content: Estrogens contribute to an additive hypercoagulable state by increasing the production of clotting factors and promoting platelet aggregation. Aminocaproic acid inhibits fibrinolysis and plasminogen activity. Amobarbital reduces the levels or effects of etonogestrel by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction requires caution and monitoring. Amoxicillin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora, which applies only to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. Antibiotics, in general, may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Ampicillin similarly decreases ethinyl estradiol levels through changes in intestinal flora, with the same considerations as amoxicillin. Aprepitant increases etonogestrel levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Armodafinil decreases etonogestrel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring similar precautions. Artemether/lumefantrine reduces etonogestrel and ethinyl estradiol levels through CYP3A4 metabolism, warranting caution and monitoring. Atazanavir increases etonogestrel levels through CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring careful monitoring. Ethinyl estradiol increases atogepant levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution. Atorvastatin increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter, requiring monitoring. Ethinyl estradiol increases axitinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution. It also increases bendamustine levels by reducing its metabolism, requiring monitoring. Bendamustine is minimally metabolized by CYP1A2, and concurrent administration with ethinyl estradiol, a weak CYP1A2 inhibitor, may increase plasma concentrations of bendamustine. Bosentan decreases etonogestrel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Butabarbital and butalbital similarly reduce etonogestrel levels through CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating monitoring. Ethinyl estradiol increases caffeine levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism, requiring caution. Cefaclor, cefadroxil, cefazolin, cefdinir, cefepime, cefepime/enmetazobactam, cefixime, cefotaxime, cefprozil, ceftazidime, ceftibuten, and cefuroxime all decrease ethinyl estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, with low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised, and alternative or additional birth control methods may be necessary. Cenobamate decreases ethinyl estradiol levels through CYP3A4 metabolism or an unspecified mechanism, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. Women should use additional or alternative non-hormonal birth control when using cenobamate with oral contraceptives. Cephalexin decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, with low risk of contraceptive failure. Ceritinib increases ethinyl estradiol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Chloramphenicol decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, with low risk of contraceptive failure. Cimetidine increases ethinyl estradiol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring monitoring. Ciprofloxacin decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, with low risk of contraceptive failure. Clarithromycin decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. Clindamycin decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, with low risk of contraceptive failure. Clobazam decreases ethinyl estradiol and etonogestrel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing hormonal contraceptive effectiveness. Additional non-hormonal contraception is recommended. Ethinyl estradiol increases clonazepam levels by reducing its metabolism, requiring caution. Ethinyl estradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines undergoing oxidation, increasing serum concentrations. Conivaptan increases etonogestrel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring monitoring. Cyclosporine increases etonogestrel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while ethinyl estradiol increases cyclosporine levels through an unknown mechanism, necessitating caution. Dabrafenib decreases ethinyl estradiol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. Darifenacin increases etonogestrel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Danicopan increases ethinyl estradiol levels through other mechanisms, requiring monitoring. Danicopan increases plasma concentrations of BCRP substrates, necessitating dose reduction of these substrates. Darunavir increases etonogestrel levels but decreases ethinyl estradiol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, reducing hormonal contraceptive efficacy. Non-hormonal contraception is recommended. Ethinyl estradiol increases dasatinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while dasatinib increases etonogestrel levels through the same pathway, requiring caution. Deferasirox decreases etonogestrel and ethinyl estradiol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring monitoring. Herbal DHEA increases etonogestrel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution. Demeclocycline decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, with low risk of contraceptive failure. Ethinyl estradiol increases diazepam levels by reducing its metabolism, requiring caution. Ethinyl estradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines undergoing oxidation, increasing serum concentrations. Dicloxacillin decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, with low risk of contraceptive failure. Doxycycline decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, with low risk of contraceptive failure. Dronedarone increases etonogestrel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Efavirenz decreases etonogestrel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating monitoring. Elafibranor decreases ethinyl estradiol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. Effective non-hormonal contraception or a barrier method is recommended during elafibranor treatment and for at least three weeks after the last dose. Elagolix decreases ethinyl estradiol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered, and consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if needed. Ethinyl estradiol increases eltrombopag levels via CYP1A2 metabolism, requiring caution. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases ethinyl estradiol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. Cobicistat, a CYP3A4 inhibitor, is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates associated with serious or life-threatening events. Encorafenib increases ethinyl estradiol levels through other mechanisms, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. Encorafenib, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase the concentration and toxicities of BCRP substrates. Erythromycin base decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, with low risk of contraceptive failure. Antibiotics may reduce hormonal contraceptive efficacy. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate similarly decrease ethinyl estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, with low risk of contraceptive failure. Etravirine decreases ethinyl estradiol and etonogestrel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Etonogestrel decreases the effects of exenatide injectable solution by pharmacodynamic antagonism, requiring caution. Estrogens may decrease the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by impairing glucose tolerance. Oral contraceptives may reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by impairing glucose tolerance. Advise patients to take oral contraceptives at least one hour before exenatide. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. Fedratinib increases ethinyl estradiol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Adjust the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. Fluconazole increases etonogestrel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Ethinyl estradiol increases finerenone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. Monitor serum potassium during initiation and dosage adjustment of either finerenone or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Adjust finerenone dosage as needed. Ethinyl estradiol increases flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Increased flibanserin adverse effects may occur if co-administered with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Fluconazole increases ethinyl estradiol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Ethinyl estradiol increases fluvoxamine levels via CYP1A2 metabolism, requiring caution. Fosamprenavir increases etonogestrel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Fosaprepitant increases etonogestrel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Fosphenytoin decreases etonogestrel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Fostemsavir increases ethinyl estradiol levels through other mechanisms, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. Fostemsavir inhibits BCRP transporters. Avoid co-administration or modify the dose of BCRP substrates co-administered with fostemsavir. Do not exceed an ethinyl estradiol dose of 30 mcg/day. Gemifloxacin decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, with low risk of contraceptive failure. Grapefruit increases etonogestrel and ethinyl estradiol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Ethinyl estradiol increases green tea levels by decreasing elimination, requiring caution. Griseofulvin decreases etonogestrel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of hemin by pharmacodynamic antagonism, requiring caution. Drugs that increase delta-aminolevulinic acid synthetase may decrease hemin effects. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of hyaluronidase through other mechanisms, requiring caution. Estrogens, when given in large systemic doses, may render tissues partially resistant to hyaluronidase action. Patients may require larger amounts of hyaluronidase for equivalent dispersing effects. Hydrocortisone decreases etonogestrel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Iloperidone increases ethinyl estradiol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may lead to increased plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. Indinavir increases etonogestrel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of insulin aspart by pharmacodynamic antagonism, requiring caution. Oral contraceptives may reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by impairing glucose tolerance. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of insulin degludec by pharmacodynamic antagonism, requiring caution. Etonogestrel decreases the effects of insulin degludec by pharmacodynamic antagonism, requiring caution. Progestins may impair glucose tolerance. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of insulin degludec/insulin aspart by pharmacodynamic antagonism, requiring caution. Etonogestrel decreases the effects of insulin degludec/insulin aspart by pharmacodynamic antagonism, requiring caution. Progestins may impair glucose tolerance. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of insulin detemir by pharmacodynamic antagonism, requiring caution. Oral contraceptives may reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by impairing glucose tolerance. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. Etonogestrel decreases the effects of inhaled insulin by pharmacodynamic antagonism, requiring caution. Progestins may impair glucose tolerance. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of insulin glargine by pharmacodynamic antagonism, requiring caution. Oral contraceptives may reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by impairing glucose tolerance. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of insulin glulisine by pharmacodynamic antagonism, requiring caution. Oral contraceptives may reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by impairing glucose tolerance. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of inhaled insulin by pharmacodynamic antagonism, requiring caution. Estrogens may impair glucose tolerance. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of insulin lispro by pharmacodynamic antagonism, requiring caution. Oral contraceptives may reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by impairing glucose tolerance. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of insulin NPH by pharmacodynamic antagonism, requiring caution. Oral contraceptives may reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by impairing glucose tolerance. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of regular human insulin by pharmacodynamic antagonism, requiring caution. Oral contraceptives may reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by impairing glucose tolerance. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. Ethinyl estradiol increases isavuconazonium sulfate levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Isoniazid increases etonogestrel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Istradefylline increases ethinyl estradiol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Istradefylline 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials. This effect was not observed with istradefylline 20 mg/day. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Itraconazole increases etonogestrel and ethinyl estradiol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. CYP3A4 inhibitors such as itraconazole may increase plasma hormone levels. Ketoconazole increases etonogestrel and ethinyl estradiol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. CYP3A4 inhibitors such as ketoconazole may increase plasma hormone levels. Etonogestrel decreases lamotrigine levels by increasing hepatic clearance, requiring caution. Ethinyl estradiol decreases lamotrigine levels by increasing hepatic clearance, requiring caution. Combination oral contraceptives significantly decrease plasma concentrations of lamotrigine, likely due to induction of lamotrigine glucuronidation. Ethinyl estradiol increases lapatinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while lapatinib increases etonogestrel levels through the same pathway, requiring caution. Ethinyl estradiol increases lemborexant levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. A lower nightly dose of lemborexant is recommended if co-administered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. See the drug monograph for specific dosage modification. Letermovir increases etonogestrel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Lenacapavir increases ethinyl estradiol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last SC dose of lenacapavir, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions of CYP3A4 substrates. Levofloxacin decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, with low risk of contraceptive failure. Levoketoconazole increases etonogestrel and ethinyl estradiol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution. CYP3A4 inhibitors such as ketoconazole may increase plasma hormone levels.
